tldr_label: TL;DR: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Iran claims a strike on a US radar in Bahrain, and Europe is set to join Ukraine talks

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and from the board. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Congress is summoning Huang over chip exports to China. [[TAG:danger:founder exits]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: The Revolutionary Guards claim they destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, and the claim is unconfirmed. Trump moved Vance off Iran talks, saying a deal is unnecessary. [[TAG:danger:escalation risk]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: After the envoys met Putin, Witkoff and Zelensky say Europeans will join the next round of talks. The Kremlin played that down, and Putin rejected foreign peacekeepers. [[TAG:warning:no date set]]

tldr_bullets.label: Washington
tldr_bullets.body: Chris Van Hollen launched a challenge to Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader ahead of a December 1 vote. [[TAG:info:leadership fight]]

tldr_bullets.label: New York
tldr_bullets.body: A building collapse in Brooklyn killed eight people, including two children. The cause is under investigation. [[TAG:danger:8 dead]]

sections.title: Nvidia After Huang
sections.summary: Founder resigns as CEO and director; CFO Kress steps in as Congress summons Huang

paragraphs.heading: Resignation
paragraphs.body: Nvidia said in a press release and SEC filing that Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO and Harvey Jones becomes the board's first chair. The board is searching for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates. NPR tied the exit to the scandal over Huang's relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The 8-K dates the board's acceptance to November 11, while the release is dated November 12. [[TAG:danger:founder exits]]

paragraphs.heading: Interim CEO
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via Investing.com, reported that Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% on Thursday before closing down 4.3%. Yahoo Finance reported that analysts generally welcomed Kress as a stabilizing choice. Some, including Dan Ives, expect the board to look outside for a permanent CEO. Kress remains CFO and will present Tuesday's earnings report. [[TAG:warning:earnings Tuesday]]

paragraphs.heading: Congress
paragraphs.body: CBS News and CNN reported that Republican committee chairs asked Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify on chip exports to China, and threatened subpoenas. Three House committees asked Huang for a closed-door interview on December 1. Engadget reported that Huang is set to testify, while other outlets said his decision was still pending. Fortune reported that Megaspeed, the company linked to the woman at the center of the scandal, is under investigation for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies. [[TAG:info:testimony sought]]

sections.title: Iran: The Lull Frays
sections.summary: Guards claim a hit on a US radar in Bahrain; Trump sidelines Vance and says no deal needed

paragraphs.heading: Bahrain Claim
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and The New Arab reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim to have struck and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, home to the US Fifth Fleet. Bahrain and the United States had not immediately confirmed the strike. The Jerusalem Post said the Guards framed it as retaliation for an attack on a telecom tower in Sirik, near the Strait of Hormuz. Reports said it is the first such claim against US assets in a Gulf state since early September. [[TAG:danger:unconfirmed strike]]

paragraphs.heading: Washington's Signals
paragraphs.body: Iran International reported that Trump told Vice President Vance to shift his focus away from Iran talks and said Washington no longer needs a deal. Israel National News reported that Trump said he could strike again without hesitation. Israel's Kan, cited by APA and World Israel News, reported that US Central Command told the Israeli military to prepare for possible renewed fighting. CENTCOM reportedly called those reports speculation. [[TAG:warning:mixed signals]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil
paragraphs.body: investingLive reported Brent near $95-96 on Friday, after an early jump of about 3%. Traders appeared to be waiting for confirmation of the Bahrain claim before adding more risk premium. [[TAG:warning:Brent near $95]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Europe at the Table?
sections.summary: Witkoff says a new round with Europeans is agreed; Kremlin downplays it; drone hits Baltic warship

paragraphs.heading: Moscow
paragraphs.body: Time and The Moscow Times reported that Witkoff and Kushner met Putin on Thursday and that Witkoff said a new round of trilateral talks was agreed. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov confirmed the talks would continue but appeared to play down Witkoff's statement that Europeans would take part. Azat TV and other outlets reported that Putin again rejected foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine and that the territorial deadlock persists. Ushakov said Putin will discuss Ukraine with Trump at the APEC summit. [[TAG:warning:deadlock persists]]

paragraphs.heading: Dublin
paragraphs.body: The Irish Times and Kyiv Independent reported that the envoys then met Zelensky at Casement Aerodrome near Dublin. Zelensky said European representatives would sit on the negotiating team directly in the next round, and that an upcoming prisoner exchange would be the largest yet. No date or venue has been announced. [[TAG:info:largest swap ahead]]

paragraphs.heading: Baltic Strike
paragraphs.body: Yahoo News and Army Recognition reported that a Ukrainian drone hit the Russian Buyan-M corvette Naro-Fominsk in the Gulf of Finland during an SBU operation against the Ust-Luga oil terminal. It was reportedly the first such attack on a Russian warship in the Baltic. Finnish officials confirmed an explosion aboard but said they could not determine who was responsible. The ship reportedly sailed to Kronstadt under its own power. [[TAG:danger:war widens north]]

sections.title: United States
sections.summary: Van Hollen challenges Schumer before a Dec. 1 vote; Brooklyn collapse kills eight

paragraphs.heading: Leadership Fight
paragraphs.body: CNN and CBS News reported that Sen. Chris Van Hollen will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader in a secret-ballot election on December 1. Reports said Van Hollen claims 'more than 10' senators back him, and that Bernie Sanders endorsed him. Schumer said he has the votes. Newsweek reported that at least six incoming senators have said they will not back Schumer. [[TAG:info:Dec 1 vote]]

paragraphs.heading: Brooklyn Collapse
paragraphs.body: NBC News and CBS New York reported that a three-story building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn collapsed on Wednesday afternoon, killing eight people and injuring at least 17. ABC News reported that the dead include two children, aged 9 and 10. Search and rescue has ended, and officials have not said what caused the collapse. [[TAG:danger:cause unknown]]

paragraphs.heading: Markets
paragraphs.body: Yahoo Finance data show the Dow fell 0.36%, the S&P 500 0.35% and the Nasdaq 0.39% on Thursday. Trading Economics cited Nvidia's leadership crisis and a rise in oil that pushed up Treasury yields. investingLive said on Friday that Fed rate-hike bets were rippling through Asia, with the US 10-year yield near 5.1%. [[TAG:warning:yields climb]]

sections.title: Israel: The Haredi Key
sections.summary: Eisenkot and Liberman greenlight outreach to Haredi parties as Netanyahu warns them off

paragraphs.heading: Outreach
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel reported that Eisenkot and Liberman approved outreach to the Haredi parties and agreed on a Knesset speaker. Yashar's Meridor said Haredi parties are welcome if they accept Eisenkot's four principles. The Jerusalem Post said Eisenkot needs both United Torah Judaism and Shas to reach 61 seats. Military service remains the main obstacle, and Haredi sources say Shas is unlikely to negotiate at all. [[TAG:warning:draft dispute]]

paragraphs.heading: Netanyahu's Warning
paragraphs.body: Yahoo News reported that Netanyahu warned the Haredi parties that Eisenkot's bloc would 'use you and throw you away.' The Times of Israel noted that any new coalition may require leaders on both sides to break campaign pledges. A minority government backed from outside by Arab parties remains a fallback that the Haredi parties and Liberman reportedly oppose. [[TAG:info:61 needed]]

sections.title: Climate and the Sahel
sections.summary: COP31's '35 by 35' electrification pledge draws an Indian refusal; Burkina's jihadists clash

paragraphs.heading: COP31 Pledge
paragraphs.body: FinChannel and The Climate Watch reported that COP31's voluntary '35 by 35' pledge aims to raise electricity to 35% of final energy use by 2035, up from roughly 20-23% today. The pledge does not require that power to be clean, which the EU has pushed for. Energy News reported that India declined to sign. A first negotiating draft is expected early next week, according to the Climate Diplomacy Brief. [[TAG:info:draft next week]]

paragraphs.heading: Burkina Faso
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and the Islamic State's Sahel affiliate are fighting each other for territory as Burkina Faso's state loses ground. The Africa Defense Forum, citing ACLED, said the clashes are the deadliest between the groups to date. Human Rights Watch documented JNIM killings of civilians and abuses by government-aligned forces. [[TAG:danger:state losing ground]]
